requirements.quote: Create a brand-new, self-signed X.509 certificate/key pair that is valid for 365 days and whose common name (CN) is dev.example.com.

check.cmd: openssl x509 -in /home/user/certs/new_server.crt -noout -subject | grep -q 'CN *= *dev.example.com' && s=$(openssl x509 -in /home/user/certs/new_server.crt -noout -subject | sed 's/^subject=//'); i=$(openssl x509 -in /home/user/certs/new_server.crt -noout -issuer | sed 's/^issuer=//'); [ "$s" = "$i" ] && openssl x509 -in /home/user/certs/new_server.crt -noout -checkend 31104000 >/dev/null && ! openssl x509 -in /home/user/certs/new_server.crt -noout -checkend 31708800 >/dev/null

requirements.quote: Create a brand-new, self-signed X.509 certificate/key pair

check.cmd: [ "$(openssl x509 -in /home/user/certs/new_server.crt -noout -pubkey | openssl sha256)" = "$(openssl pkey -in /home/user/certs/new_server.key -pubout | openssl sha256)" ]

requirements.quote: They must arrive in the archive directory with their original file names intact (i.e., /home/user/certs/archive/server.crt and /home/user/certs/archive/server.key).
After the move, there should no longer be files named server.crt or server.key in /home/user/certs.
Exact format: **four lines, no extra spaces, each terminated by a single newline character**
The specific date must be generated at runtime with the local system’s `date +%F` output
While you are at it, clear out `/srv/nectar` so that directory no longer exists; the host is short on disk space.
